row.evidence: GitLab's SCIM docs for GitLab.com groups and for Self-Managed are both marked "Tier: Premium, Ultimate", and Premium, the lowest paid plan, is $29 per user/month billed annually on the pricing page.
row.notes: Status changed from gated (June) to free by classification, not by a price change: Premium ($29/u/mo annual) is both GitLab's lowest paid tier and the lowest SCIM tier, so under the price-gate rule there is no SCIM upcharge over the team plan. Free (5 users per top-level group) has no SCIM. The pricing page itself does not mention SCIM or SAML; the tier comes from the docs. GitLab.com group SCIM requires group SAML SSO, supports create, deactivate (removes group membership; the GitLab.com account is kept) and reactivate; the docs say it doesn't support updating users, and SCIM group provisioning is not supported on GitLab.com. Self-Managed/Dedicated instance SCIM (Premium) blocks users on deprovision and supports SCIM Groups via SAML group links (GitLab 18.0+). Okta needs Okta Lifecycle Management. Members API is on all tiers; Audit events API, group member webhooks and the Enterprise users API are Premium+.

plans.name: Free
plans.price_text: $0 per user/month; 5 users per top-level group

auth.token_source: GitLab.com: top-level group > Settings > SAML SSO > Generate a SCIM token (shown with the SCIM API endpoint URL). Self-Managed: Admin area SCIM token.

endpoints.notes: Groups endpoints exist only on the Self-Managed/Dedicated instance SCIM API (SAML group links); GitLab.com group SCIM has Users only and SCIM group provisioning is not supported.

operations.notes: PATCH updates id/externalId, name.formatted, emails, active and userName per the internal API reference, although the setup page says SCIM doesn't support updating users (see conflicts). DELETE on the group SCIM API removes the SCIM identity/membership, not the GitLab account. Instance SCIM supports group create/replace/patch/delete for SAML-group-linked groups (group_push true on Self-Managed only).

deprovision.data_retained: GitLab.com: user is removed from the top-level group, subgroups and projects; the GitLab.com account is not deleted and the linked SAML identity remains. Removal is processed asynchronously. Self-Managed: the user is blocked (identity active: false) and the SCIM identity stays linked.

pagination.notes: startIndex and count, per the SCIM spec.

roles.how: SCIM-provisioned users get the group's default membership role from SAML SSO settings; when restricted access applies and no seats are free, users get the Minimal Access role, reflected in the roles attribute. Self-Managed maps IdP groups to GitLab groups via SAML group links.

limitations.text: GitLab.com group SCIM does not support SCIM group provisioning; disable group provisioning in Entra.
Okta SCIM requires the Okta Lifecycle Management product.
Only tested identity providers are supported; others may work but are unsupported.
The SCIM API is an internal API for SCIM provider integration and may change without notice.

capabilities.notes: Creating users (POST /users) is administrator-only on Self-Managed/Dedicated. On GitLab.com, group owners manage membership (and, on Premium+, enterprise users).

endpoints.purpose: Remove a billable member from a group

events: Group member events: member added, access level changed, access expiry updated, member removed (Premium+)

rate_limits.text: Instance audit events API is subject to a configurable per-user rate limit.

okta.notes: OIN GitLab app lists SCIM, Create, Deactivate; GitLab's docs say the catalogue app does not support SAML, so SSO uses a separate SAML app.

entra.notes: GitLab's docs set Entra up as a non-gallery application for SAML and point its provisioning at the GitLab SCIM endpoint (generic SCIM).

google.notes: GitLab documents Google Workspace for group SAML SSO only; Google Workspace is not among the SCIM providers configured in GitLab's SCIM docs. Google's own catalogue was not checked.

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP group sync and SAML Group Sync (Self-Managed / group SAML)
